# ProjectSetup

**Class** · namespace `VRFramework.Core.Editors.Setup` · assembly `VRFramework.Core.Editors` · [view source](https://git.cie-group.cz/vr-framework/vrf4/core/-/blob/main/Editor/Setup/ProjectSetup.cs#L20)

Everything the setup writes into the project itself: the framework's own template assets, the
project settings a VR build needs, the two StreamingAssets files the platform reads on start,
and the shared .gitignore that is fetched rather than shipped.
Each method here is one step of [`PackageSetup`](/api/vrframework-core-editors-setup/PackageSetup) and each is safe to run twice - a
setup that can only be run on a virgin project is a setup nobody dares run.

```csharp
public static class ProjectSetup
```

### ConfigureGraphicsAndQuality() {#configuregraphicsandquality}

### ConfigurePlayerSettings() {#configureplayersettings}

The player settings a Quest or Pico build will not work without, plus the framework's
splash screen. Identity - company, product, version - is only filled in while it is still
Unity's default, so re-running this on a real project does not rename the app.

### CreateStreamingAssets() {#createstreamingassets}

Writes the two files the platform reads on start, and marks the framework settings asset as
set up. Existing files are left as they are: they hold what a project has already
described about itself.

```csharp
public static void CreateStreamingAssets()
```

[View source](https://git.cie-group.cz/vr-framework/vrf4/core/-/blob/main/Editor/Setup/ProjectSetup.cs#L368)

### FetchGitignore() {#fetchgitignore}

Starts the download of the framework's .gitignore. The file lands at the project root, next
to Assets and Packages, which is where git looks for it and is above everything Unity
considers an asset - so it is written with File rather than through the asset database.

```csharp
public static void FetchGitignore()
```

[View source](https://git.cie-group.cz/vr-framework/vrf4/core/-/blob/main/Editor/Setup/ProjectSetup.cs#L416)

### GitignoreFetched() {#gitignorefetched}

Polled by the runner until the download is over, and the place the file is actually
written. A machine with no network ends up with a reported failure and a setup that
carried on: nothing else in the project depends on this file existing.

### SwitchToAndroid() {#switchtoandroid}

Switches to Android, which is where every headset build goes. Unity recompiles for the new
platform, so this is a step of its own with the rest of the sequence waiting behind it.
